Logline

A young woman hunting her boyfriend’s killer uncovers an Aztec death cult beneath an elite racquet club — and she’s its next queen.

The Story

Every family has a tradition.

Seattle. Weeks before her eighteenth birthday, Kracell is heir to the Sneer Racquet Club, the old-money tennis club her family has run for a hundred years.

Then her boyfriend Bobby is taken from his bedroom in the middle of the night. The police already have their man: a Native American stranger found on a roadside, framed and jailed for a string of disappearances that only ever take children of color, the cases no one in power seems to want solved.

Kracell starts hunting. The deeper she digs, the closer it gets to home: to the courts, to the jade her family never takes off, and to the New Year’s Eve celebration they have been preparing her for since the day she was born.

Genre Supernatural horror Setting Seattle, present day Shoot Seattle area, 2027
I — THE CLUB

A hundred years of membership. No one ever really leaves.

II — THE WATCHERS

Someone is always at the fence line.

III — THE MISSING

Children whose names no one says.

IV — BENEATH

Under the courts, something has been kept fed.

V — THE JUBILEE

Every fifty years, the club crowns a queen.

Why This Film

Blood Court is a supernatural horror film about who gets to live forever, and who pays for it.
Giving up is not innocence.
It is how the system survives.

Blood Court is about racism and classism. Young people of color go missing while the people with the power to stop it look away, not because they can’t act, but because acting is hard and they have made peace with the way things are. The horror is the status quo.

It is also about what happens when culture is taken. At the heart of the film is a Mexica god stolen centuries ago and put to work keeping a wealthy family young. A sacred rite becomes a beauty treatment. A people’s faith becomes someone else’s inheritance.

The film is made with care for the cultures it draws on. Its Indigenous characters are written as full, contemporary people, not mystical guides, and a Nahua cultural and language consultant joins the team before the script is locked.

ExclusionWho the system overlooks, and who it decides not to see.
ExcellenceGenre craft at the level of the films that defined it.
RecognitionStories from the margins, made for the mainstream.

Son of a Botanist Productions — named for a father who spent his life naming living things

The World

What the members pay for.

Founded 1925

The Club

The Sneer Racquet Club: clay courts, a waiting list, and members who never seem to get older.

For the queen

The Necklace

Carved jade, worn by one woman at a time. It has never been taken off.

For the family

The Bracelets

Given to the family and its leaders. Time is gentler to the people who wear them.

Beneath the courts

The God

Stolen from Mexico centuries ago, chained in the dark and fed. It chooses its own heirs.

The Blood Court Films

One family. One hundred years.

A feature and two standalone prequel shorts, each set at a turning point in the Sneer family’s fifty-year cycle, plus the teaser that introduces the world.

The Team

Who’s making it.

Director

Tierra “TT” Frost

Seattle born and raised, MFA in directing from Chapman University’s Dodge College. Her short JUK won the ASC Heritage Award, earned an Out on Film grant, was a PBS Fine Cut semi-finalist, screened with Oxford, MACRO and Chapman, and ran on a Sunset Boulevard billboard. She also directed I Can See The Light. TT leads the creative vision across every Blood Court film.

Writer · Producer

Marc Sternberg

Writer and lead producer. Creator of Blood Court: he wrote the original short story and screenplay, the v1-2 and v1-3 rewrites, both prequel shorts and the teaser. Produces through Son of a Botanist Productions. MFA (Chapman), MSc (HEC Paris/Oxford), MBA (Arizona), MA (Northern Arizona) and Fulbright Specialist, after 20 years as a marketing executive and entrepreneur. Producer of the feature documentaries Unknown Country and Cowgirls: Women of Western Art, and of TT Frost’s JUK.

Producer

Thao Phan

Seattle-based producer on Blood Court and BLOOD JUBILEE, rooting the films in the Seattle community where they will be made.

Director of Photography

Sandra Garcia

Seattle-based cinematographer and camera operator (Alma Mía Productions), passionate about stories that center underrepresented communities. Narrative, music video, documentary and commercial work, including for Seattle Pride, Amazon and Microsoft.

Screenplay

Saul Espinoza

Mexican American screenwriter with an MFA in screenwriting from Chapman. Wrote the first draft of Blood Court.

Screenplay

Edith Storm

Sweden-based horror writer: Slamdance top three, Best Feature in Berlin. Writing the rewrite to the shooting draft, and co-writer of the teaser.

Composer & Music Supervisor

Octaviano Rogés

Composer of TT Frost’s JUK, scoring the Blood Court world.

Creative Consultant

Dawit Borrows

Seattle-based writer-director, producer and photographer, founder of Tambia Productions.

Story Consultant

Tania Violeta Sternberg

Story and cultural consultant on the Blood Court films.

Development

From short story to shooting draft.

January 2024

“Kracell and the Crystal”

Marc Sternberg’s original short story, where Kracell and her world begin. U.S. Copyright Reg. TX 9-359-566, effective January 30, 2024.

June 2024

Tennis Court Dungeons, Part One

Marc’s first feature screenplay from the story (126 pages). U.S. Copyright Reg. PA 2-482-005, effective June 27, 2024; WGA East Registry No. I371639.

February 2025

Blood Court, draft v1

First draft under the Blood Court title, written by Saul Espinoza on commission.

2025 – 2026

Drafts v1-2 and v1-3

Two full rewrites by Marc Sternberg. Draft v1-3 (July 11, 2026) is the 137-scene draft that the package is built on.

August 2026

Every draft filed

Copyright applications for drafts v1, v1-2 and v1-3 filed with the U.S. Copyright Office, effective August 25, 2026.

October 2026

Teaser shot · rewrite underway

The teaser is shot on October 3. Edith Storm delivers her first rewrite (v1-4), and BLOOD JUBILEE is submitted for grant funding.

November – December 2026

Draft v1-5, then the final draft

An updated draft, a final round of notes, and the final draft in December, at about 95–100 pages.

2027

Production in Seattle

BLOOD JUBILEE shoots first, no earlier than May. The Blood Court feature follows in the fall.

Rights

Blood Court is an original story by Marc Sternberg, based on his registered short story and feature screenplay. The writers who joined after the story was created were engaged under written agreements.
